correctness.rationale: Analytical proof specifies all parameter and boundary conditions. Direct substitution gives the unique positive equilibrium \(E\); the Jacobian discriminant is \(D(\kappa)=(A-\kappa B)^2-4\kappa C\). The exact positive identity \(X^2-B^2D=4(\tau-1)C\) establishes the unique spectral-rate optimum at \(\kappa_+\), while a different one-variable derivative establishes the maximum frequency-to-damping ratio at \(\kappa_0\). For every \(\kappa_b>\kappa_0\), strict negative spectral separation from \(-A\) holds for complex, real and defective repeated eigenvalues. The focus trajectory has a nonzero \(e^{-At}\) cosine coefficient for initial deviation \((\varepsilon,0)\), whereas the comparison solution is \(o(e^{-At})\), proving infinitely many genuine nonlinear sign-changing crossings. The 245 exact-rational parameter cases and direct finite-time integrations corroborate but do not replace these infinite proofs. The rate is explicitly an asymptotic spectral exponent, allowing Jordan-block prefactors.

value.rationale: With ratio omega fixed, mean endemic burden is insensitive to changing the speed of link turnover. The complete three-regime node/focus spectrum shows this invariance hides a substantive temporal distinction. The optimal local damping speed differs from the optimal relative oscillation speed, and the mathematically unavoidable indefinitely repeated but shrinking prevalence ranking reversals demonstrate limits of finite-time policy comparisons. Both strict optima and the exact infinite-crossing theorem give motivated quantified new structure, not a merely recomputed sample Jacobian.
